question: How can user modeling techniques be improved to capture and leverage individual preferences more effectively in personalized recommendation systems?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer must explain that particle binding to a high-Q optical microcavity perturbs the cavity mode at resonance wavelength λ0, producing a resonance shift δλ that changes cavity transmission, and that this mechanism underlies most current microcavity sensors.
examples: Binding of a particle to a high-Q microcavity perturbs the cavity mode, causing a resonance shift δλ that alters transmission
The dominant microcavity sensing principle is detecting δλ induced by analyte binding

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer must state that sensing resolution depends critically on the optical quality factor Q, with higher Q (narrower linewidths) enabling finer resolvable shifts.
examples: Sensing resolution is critically dependent on the optical quality factor Q
Higher Q resonances filter spectral noise more effectively, improving the smallest resolvable shift

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer must cite the highest reported resolution, δλ/λ0 = 3×10^-10, achieved with an optical Q of 10^8 at a visible wavelength in an aqueous environment.
examples: The best reported resolution is δλ/λ0 = 3×10^-10 using Q = 10^8 at visible wavelength in water
Highest resolution: fractional shift 3×10^-10, visible wavelength, aqueous

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer must note that even this state-of-the-art resolution still exceeds the shift induced by a single protein binding event, motivating further enhancement for single-protein detection.
examples: Even 3×10^-10 exceeds the shift from a single protein binding, so single-protein detection remains out of reach
The record resolution is insufficient for direct single-protein detection

ingredients.name: answer_critical_4
ingredients.criterion: The answer must identify that detecting single proteins down to 1 kDa requires adding a plasmonic nanoantenna to the microcavity to enhance the resonance wavelength shift, at the cost of significantly reducing the effective detection area.
examples: A plasmonic nanoantenna on the microcavity amplifies the shift, enabling 1 kDa single-protein detection but shrinking the detection area
Plasmonic enhancement boosts sensitivity to single small proteins at the price of a much smaller effective sensing area

ingredients.name: answer_critical_5
ingredients.criterion: The answer must present cavity optomechanics as an approach that dramatically enhances WGM sensor resolution without compromising the effective detection area, avoiding the trade-off of plasmonic approaches.
examples: Cavity optomechanics enhances resolution by orders of magnitude while preserving the full detection area
Optomechanics offers area-preserving resolution enhancement for WGM sensors

ingredients.name: answer_critical_6
ingredients.criterion: The answer must explain that blue-detuned laser excitation drives radiation-pressure-induced regenerative optomechanical oscillation (OMO) with a narrow linewidth, whose microwave-range frequency depends on laser-cavity detuning, so molecular binding perturbations of the optical resonance are transferred to the mechanical frequency.
examples: Radiation pressure from blue-detuned driving produces coherent narrow-linewidth OMO; binding events shift the OMO frequency
OMO frequency tracks laser-cavity detuning, so resonance perturbations become microwave-frequency shifts

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer should note that optomechanical sensing resolution scales with both the optical Q and the effective mechanical Q of the OMO, yielding up to six orders of magnitude resolution enhancement sufficient for single-molecule detection.
examples: Resolution depends on optical Q and OMO mechanical Q, improving by six orders of magnitude
Dual dependence on optical and mechanical Q yields ~10^6 improvement, enough for single molecules

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer should cite Lu et al.'s experiment in which BSA (66 kDa) binding/unbinding in DPBS produced discrete oscillation-frequency steps with a signal-to-noise ratio of 16.8, demonstrating single-molecule detection.
examples: Lu et al. observed discrete frequency steps corresponding to single BSA (66 kDa) binding events with SNR 16.8
Stepwise OMO frequency changes from single BSA molecules in buffer validated the method

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer should explicitly contrast the two enhancement strategies — plasmonic nanoantenna versus cavity optomechanics — in terms of resolution gain versus effective detection area.
examples: Plasmonic enhancement trades area for shift enhancement; optomechanics enhances resolution without this trade-off
Comparing the two routes: nanoantenna reduces detection area, optomechanics does not
